messages:
Priya S: quick note: onboarding 'aether-liteq' (int4, streaming on) showed a spike in funcall parse errors specifically where responses end with a short invisible suffix. stack trace points to our strict ndjson parser bailing.
Liam K: can you paste an example? even a redacted one helps.
Priya S: example below (copied raw):
```
{"action":"invoke","tool":"lookup_user","args":{"uid":"u-12345"}}
�
```
That trailing control bytes seem to appear ~0.9% of calls on the canary.
ops-bot: canary run aether-liteq-int4-2026-03-22: parse_fail_rate=0.92%, baseline aether-int8=0.05%
Liam K: interesting. wonder if quantized kernels emit different eos token sequences or if streaming frame boundaries are off. did you try with kv_cache disabled?
Priya S: turning kvcache off drops failures to 0.08% but latency goes up. So it's likely kvcache+streaming interaction.
Liam K: ok. short-term patch idea: extend our funcall postprocessor to strip trailing C0 control chars (<=0x1F) and then attempt ndjson-repair heuristics. add one-off telemetry dimension 'suffix_control_bytes' for slices. low-risk and reversible.
Priya S: let's do that as a hotfix in canary parser and enable verbose dump for a sample of failures (first 200). also add an assert in the tokenizer alignment tests to catch malformed eos sequences on quant kernels.
canary-bot: scheduled mirror: aether-liteq-int4/mirror/30k (kvcache=on) starting now.
Liam K: long-term: we should test tokenizer/decoder alignment across quant kernels with artificially-constructed eos-adjacent sequences. maybe add a deterministic seed test in the kernel CI that runs streaming + kvcache combo.
Priya S: agreed. Action items: Liam -> implement postprocess strip + telemetry, Priya -> enable dumps and run mirror, Ops -> watch canary.
Liam K: I'll open a short RFC for the kernel CI test and link here when ready. :thumbsup:
Priya S: thanks, will follow up with mirror results in ~90min.
Liam K: thumbs.
